title: fix(plugin-calendar): object-calendar reads the allDayField it resolves
body:
Fixes #8026

`ObjectCalendar` now reads the `allDayField` it was already resolving. Direction 1, per the triage routing comment.

## What was wrong

`getCalendarConfig` put `allDayField` into the config it returns and the config memo named the key among its dependencies; the events pass then destructured four keys and computed the flag as `!endDate`. So an author who wrote `calendar: { allDayField: 'is_all_day' }` got the flag derived from whether the record happened to carry an end date, and **a record with a real end date that IS flagged all-day drew as an ordinary timed event, with no diagnostic.**

The value was arriving. `ListView`'s `collectViewFields` already puts this field into the fetch, and `ObjectView`'s `calendarViewOptions` forwards the authored `calendar` block verbatim — so the flag was queried from the backend, delivered on the record, and dropped at the last step.

## The no-key decision, and why it is not the sibling's

The triage asked for this to be decided explicitly rather than inherited. It is:

- **`allDayField` declared** — that field is the whole answer. `Boolean(record[allDayField])`. A record whose flag is absent or false is **not** all-day; letting the inference run behind a declared key would silently overrule the author, which is this card's own defect inverted.
- **`allDayField` absent** — nothing changes. The existing `!endDate` inference stands, unmodified, and every calendar that never authored the key renders exactly as it did before.

**No `|| 'allDay'` default is taken**, and that is the one deliberate divergence from the `calendar-view` sibling. The argument is measured, not stylistic:

1. This renderer honours **none** of the sibling's five field-name defaults. `titleField`, `endDateField` and `colorField` all read the authored name or nothing, and an absent `startDateField` reaches the refusal screen rather than a guess — objectui#7029, ruled objectstack#13748 batch 19 option A, whose entire content was deleting fabricated field bindings upstream. Importing one of five would put the last guess back into the one file whose refusal screen exists to refuse guessing.
2. The sibling's defaults describe the canonical **authored event** shape a `calendar-view` node literally carries in its `data` array. `object-calendar` draws ObjectQL records of a business object, where nothing makes `allDay` a field name.
3. **The cost is measured, not asserted.** Ablation leg B below ports the sibling verbatim and turns two rows red — including a calendar with a `startDateField` and no `endDateField`, a documented shipped shape, which stops rendering its events as all-day. That is the behaviour change the triage warned about, quantified.

## Premise check — three of the card's four faces are faces of a different component

The card and the triage both rest on "declared, documented, spec-declared, sibling-honoured". Re-measured on this tree, that reads differently, and the report on the card carries the full evidence. In short:

- **"Declared, and by the spec" is false.** `@objectstack/spec`'s `CalendarConfigSchema` is a `strictObject` of exactly four keys and refuses `allDayField` **by name**, with an `unrecognized_keys` diagnostic — on the pinned 17.3.0 and on objectstack `main`. Three independent instruments agree: a runtime `safeParse` (with `bogusKeyXy` and objectui's own `defaultView` as lit controls, both refused identically), the schema source, and TypeScript, which prints the type as `{ startDateField; endDateField?; titleField?; colorField? }` when the local widening is removed.
- The `@default 'allDay'` doc comment and the README lines the card cites belong to **`CalendarViewSchema`**, the sibling `calendar-view` element's own type. The `object-calendar` half of that README documents no `allDayField`.
- **"Plumbed" is true but misattributed.** The cited flat-key list is a dev-mode warning, not a flattening; the real route is `calendarViewOptions` forwarding the nested `calendar` block verbatim.

**None of that weakens the fix — it relocates its basis, and the relocated basis is stronger.** `allDayField` is an objectui-**local** extension of `CalendarConfig`, in exactly the class objectui's sanctioned `defaultView` already occupies (the spec refuses `defaultView` on this object in the identical shape, and this renderer has honoured it for releases). Two faces say so in as many words:

- `packages/types/src/zod/objectql.zod.ts` keeps `.passthrough()` on the `CalendarConfig` mirror deliberately and names this key: "the renderers grow config knobs ahead of the protocol (calendar's `allDayField`, for one), and stripping them here would silently disable a shipped capability."
- `packages/types/src/designer.ts` declares `calendar: { startDateField, endDateField, titleField, colorField, allDayField, defaultView }` — the **designer offers the author this input**, next to `defaultView`. Neither the card nor the triage found this one, and it moves the grade's own re-grade condition: this is not only "an author who sets it", it is an author the designer invites to set it.

So this PR widens no accept set. objectui's published validator already admits the key, `ListView` already fetches it, `ObjectView` already forwards it, the designer already offers it, and `ObjectCalendar` already resolved it. The only missing rung was the read.

## Evidence

Pinned by **rendered behaviour** — which lane `CalendarView` draws the bar in — never by asserting the key appears in the config object. `CalendarView` has its own all-day classifier on top of `event.allDay` (midnight-to-midnight, or 24h or longer), so every fixture sits **outside** it: 09:00 to 10:30 on one day, neither boundary midnight. The flag is then the only thing deciding the lane. Timed bars carry the same `title` attribute as all-day bars, so the title cannot discriminate; the lane can, and it exists in the DOM only when at least one event is classified all-day.

Six rows: the defect; a falsy-flag control (so "always all-day" cannot pass); a control proving the field read is the **declared** one and not a fixed name; the no-default pin; and two MUST-NOT-CHANGE rows for the untouched inference.

**Ablation, both legs from the committed fix, each restored to the HEAD blob hash with `git diff HEAD` empty:**

| leg | mutation | result |
|---|---|---|
| A | back to `allDay: !endDate` | 1 failed, 5 passed — only THE DEFECT row goes red |
| B | verbatim sibling port with the `allDay` default | 2 failed, 4 passed — the no-default pin **and** the no-end-date MUST-NOT-CHANGE row go red |

Each mutation was proved on disk before the run (anchor occurrences 1 to 0, injected 0 to 1, blob hash differing from HEAD), and each restore proved by blob-hash equality plus an empty `git diff HEAD`, not by an exit code.

**Reverse verification of the type claim:** returning the plain spec `CalendarConfig` from `getCalendarConfig` makes `tsc` red at the destructure with `TS2339: Property 'allDayField' does not exist on type '{ startDateField: string; endDateField?: string; titleField?: string; colorField?: string; }'`, then green again on restore.

**Gates** (derived by hand — `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` is objectstack-only and does not exist here):

| gate | exit |
|---|---|
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-calendar/` | 0 — 32 files, 226 tests, includes the objectui#7711 memo pin |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-calendar run type-check` | 0 — both `tsc --noEmit` and `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-calendar lint` | 0 — 38 files, 0 errors, 226 pre-existing warnings |
| `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/plugin-calendar^...' build` | 0 |
| `check:control-bytes` `check:vi-mock-specifiers` `check:vi-mock-inherit` `check:handler-key-reads` `check:spec-symbols` `check:phantom-deps` `check:self-import` `check:unreferenced-sources` `check:element-data-source-declaration` `check:side-effects-array` `check:doc-example-readers` `check:doc-types` `check:i18n-keys` `check:i18n-drift` `check:i18n-dead-keys` | 0 |
| `check-changeset-presence` / `check-changeset-no-major` | 0 |
| adjacent: `ListView.calendar-binding-7029` + `ObjectView.calendarBinding-7029` + `list-view-spec-parity` | 0 — 35 tests |

Three gates report **PRECONDITION NOT MET (exit 2)**, which their own output distinguishes from a finding: `check:sdui-registration-pins`, `check:eager-closure` (both need an `apps/console` build) and `check:doc-snippets` (needs a 34-package scoped build). Left to CI, with the narrowing declared: this diff touches **zero** `export` lines (grep of the diff), no `.md`, no `ComponentRegistry.register` call, no `sideEffects` array, and adds no module import to any source file — so the published type surface, the bundle chunk graph and the registration arrays those three weigh cannot have moved. Type-aware linting is not enabled in `eslint.config.js` (no `project` / `projectService`), so the package-scoped lint run cannot have a different verdict on any untouched file.

## 验收备注

Two observations, neither filed as a card, neither touched here:

- `OBJECT_CALENDAR_INPUTS` in `index.tsx` describes the `calendar` input as "startDateField, endDateField, titleField, colorField" — it omits `allDayField`. A description string, outside this claim's file surface; noted, not filed.
- `allDayField` rides objectui's `.passthrough()` anonymously rather than being a declared local extension the way `defaultView` is (`objectql.zod.ts`'s `.extend({})` and `list-view-spec-parity.test.ts`'s sanctioned-local list). Now that the key is honoured, a future hardening of that `.passthrough()` would silently drop a shipped capability — the class objectui#15469 recorded for gantt. **Deliberately not filed as its own card:** its whole content dissolves if the upstream spec gap lands, so it is carried as a line on that card instead.
